Lemma
1. ch8:8.11

Let $V$ be an inner product space, $W$ a vector space, and $B,B':V\times V\to W$ symmetric bilinear maps. If $B(v,v)=B'(v,v)$ for every unit vector $v$, then $B=B'$.

Proof

\sketch Homogeneity extends the diagonal equality to every $v\in V$. Polarization then gives

\[ B(v,w)=\frac14\bigl(B(v+w,v+w)-B(v-w,v-w)\bigr), \]

and the same identity for $B'$ proves equality.

□

A Riemannian submanifold $(M,g)$ of $(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ is totally geodesic if every ambient geodesic tangent to $M$ at a time $t_0$ remains in $M$ on some interval about $t_0$.
